preamble.title: Preamble
preamble.subtitle: Constitutional philosophy
preamble.core: Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic; Justice, Liberty, Equality and Fraternity. The Preamble guides constitutional interpretation.
points: 42nd Amendment added ‘Socialist’, ‘Secular’ and ‘integrity’.
Kesavananda Bharati: Preamble is part of the Constitution.
Not an independent source of power, but an interpretive guide.
preamble.upsc: Link Preamble values to constitutional morality, welfare state, secularism, democracy and dignity.

part1.title: Part I — Union and its Territory
part1.subtitle: Articles 1–4
part1.core: India, that is Bharat, is a Union of States. Parliament has broad power to admit, establish or reorganise States.
points: Art. 1: name and territory.
Art. 3: formation/alteration of States; President's recommendation required.
State legislature's view is sought but is not binding on Parliament.
part1.upsc: Frequently tested distinction: constitutional amendment under Art. 368 is not required for laws under Arts. 2–4.

part2.title: Part II — Citizenship
part2.subtitle: Articles 5–11
part2.core: Part II dealt primarily with citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution; Parliament may regulate citizenship by law.
points: Art. 11 enables Parliament to legislate on citizenship.
Citizenship Act, 1955 is central to present statutory rules.
Constitution provides single citizenship for India.
part2.upsc: Separate constitutional provisions at commencement from current statutory citizenship rules.

part3.title: Part III — Fundamental Rights
part3.subtitle: Articles 12–35
part3.core: Justiciable rights restrain State action and protect liberty, equality, religious freedom, cultural/educational rights and constitutional remedies.
points: Art. 14 equality; 19 freedoms; 21 life & personal liberty.
Art. 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during an Emergency under Art. 359.
Art. 32: right to constitutional remedies; Supreme Court writ jurisdiction.
part3.upsc: Always connect Art. 14 + 19 + 21 (‘golden triangle’), reasonable restrictions, positive obligations and judicial review.

part4.title: Part IV — Directive Principles
part4.subtitle: Articles 36–51
part4.core: Non-justiciable principles directing the State toward social and economic democracy and a welfare state.
points: Art. 38 social order; 39 socio-economic principles; 39A free legal aid.
Art. 44 Uniform Civil Code; 48A environment; 50 separation of judiciary from executive.
FR–DPSP harmony is part of constitutional balance.
part4.upsc: Mains favorite: tension and harmony between individual rights and socio-economic transformation.

part4a.title: Part IVA — Fundamental Duties
part4a.subtitle: Article 51A
part4a.core: Eleven Fundamental Duties guide civic responsibility; most are not directly enforceable unless supported by law.
points: Added by 42nd Amendment (1976), originally 10 duties.
86th Amendment added parent/guardian duty concerning education of children 6–14.
Can inform interpretation of laws and reasonable restrictions.
part4a.upsc: Useful in Ethics, environment, scientific temper and citizenship answers.

part5.title: Part V — The Union
part5.subtitle: Articles 52–151
part5.core: Union executive, Parliament, legislative procedure, Supreme Court and CAG.
points: President: constitutional head; Council of Ministers aids and advises.
Parliament = President + Rajya Sabha + Lok Sabha.
Supreme Court: constitutional adjudication and judicial review; CAG audits public finances.
part5.upsc: Break this Part into Executive, Parliament, Judiciary and CAG for revision.

part6.title: Part VI — The States
part6.subtitle: Articles 152–237
part6.core: State executive, legislatures, High Courts and subordinate courts.
points: Governor is constitutional head of State.
Arts. 163–164: Council of Ministers headed by CM.
High Courts have broader writ reach under Art. 226 than SC under Art. 32 in subject matter.
part6.upsc: Governor’s discretion, assent to Bills and Centre–State friction are recurring GS-II themes.

part8.title: Part VIII — Union Territories
part8.subtitle: Articles 239–242
part8.core: Union Territories are administered under a constitutionally distinct framework; some have legislatures and Councils of Ministers.
points: Art. 239: administration of UTs.
Art. 239AA: special provisions for NCT of Delhi.
Legislative powers vary by UT.
part8.upsc: Delhi federalism and LG–elected government disputes are important contemporary constitutional themes.

part9.title: Part IX — Panchayats
part9.subtitle: Articles 243–243O
part9.core: Constitutional framework for rural local self-government.
points: 73rd Amendment; constitutional status to Panchayats.
Three-tier structure subject to population exceptions.
Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects.
part9.upsc: Revise reservations, State Election Commission, State Finance Commission and Gram Sabha.

part9a.title: Part IXA — Municipalities
part9a.subtitle: Articles 243P–243ZG
part9a.core: Constitutional framework for urban local self-government.
points: 74th Amendment; Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Council, Municipal Corporation.
Twelfth Schedule lists 18 functions.
Ward Committees and metropolitan/district planning matter for urban governance.
part9a.upsc: Strong overlap with GS-II governance and GS-I urbanisation.

part9b.title: Part IXB — Co-operative Societies
part9b.subtitle: Articles 243ZH–243ZT
part9b.core: Constitutional provisions relating to co-operative societies.
points: Inserted by the 97th Amendment.
Supreme Court (2021) invalidated the amendment insofar as it governed State co-operatives without required State ratification; provisions continue in relation to multi-State co-operatives.
Art. 43B in DPSP and co-operative freedom under Art. 19(1)(c) were also introduced.
part9b.upsc: Useful for federalism + co-operative movement questions.

part10.title: Part X — Scheduled & Tribal Areas
part10.subtitle: Articles 244–244A
part10.core: Special administration of Scheduled and Tribal Areas through the Fifth and Sixth Schedules.
points: Fifth Schedule: Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes outside Sixth Schedule areas.
Sixth Schedule: autonomous arrangements in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
Art. 244A permits an autonomous State framework within Assam.
part10.upsc: Know Fifth vs Sixth Schedule differences.

part11.title: Part XI — Union–State Relations
part11.subtitle: Articles 245–263
part11.core: Legislative and administrative relations between Union and States.
points: Art. 246 + Seventh Schedule distribute legislative subjects.
Arts. 249, 250, 252, 253 allow Parliament to legislate in special circumstances.
Art. 263: Inter-State Council.
part11.upsc: Core federalism chapter: legislative competence, repugnancy, inter-governmental coordination.

part12.title: Part XII — Finance, Property, Contracts & Suits
part12.subtitle: Articles 264–300A
part12.core: Public finance, taxation, Finance Commission, borrowing, government property/contracts and right to property.
points: Art. 265: no tax except by authority of law.
Art. 280: Finance Commission.
Art. 300A: property is a constitutional/legal right, not a Fundamental Right.
part12.upsc: Link Finance Commission and GST-era fiscal federalism to constitutional design.

part13.title: Part XIII — Trade, Commerce & Intercourse
part13.subtitle: Articles 301–307
part13.core: Freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse across India, subject to constitutional restrictions.
points: Art. 301 gives the general freedom.
Parliament and States may impose constitutionally permitted restrictions.
Important for economic unity and federal market questions.
part13.upsc: Less frequent, but useful for conceptual federalism/economic-union MCQs.

part14.title: Part XIV — Services
part14.subtitle: Articles 308–323
part14.core: Services under Union and States and Public Service Commissions.
points: Art. 309 recruitment/service conditions.
Art. 310 doctrine of pleasure, subject to safeguards.
Art. 311 safeguards civil servants against dismissal/removal/reduction in rank.
part14.upsc: Directly relevant to civil-service neutrality, accountability and safeguards.

part14a.title: Part XIVA — Tribunals
part14a.subtitle: Articles 323A–323B
part14a.core: Constitutional basis for administrative and other tribunals.
points: Added by 42nd Amendment.
323A: administrative tribunals.
323B: tribunals for specified matters.
part14a.upsc: Judicial independence, tribunal reform and High Court review are recurring issues.

part15.title: Part XV — Elections
part15.subtitle: Articles 324–329
part15.core: Constitutional architecture for elections, centred on the Election Commission of India.
points: Art. 324: superintendence, direction and control of elections.
Art. 325: one general electoral roll; no exclusion on listed identity grounds.
Art. 326: adult suffrage.
part15.upsc: Connect ECI independence, MCC (statutory vs non-statutory aspects), disqualification and electoral reforms.

part16.title: Part XVI — Special Provisions for Certain Classes
part16.subtitle: Articles 330–342A
part16.core: Representation and constitutional identification/safeguards concerning SCs, STs and socially/educationally backward classes.
points: Political reservation for SC/ST in legislatures.
Arts. 338, 338A, 338B: constitutional commissions.
Arts. 341, 342 and 342A concern specification of SC/ST/SEBC.
part16.upsc: Pair constitutional commissions with their Articles.

part17.title: Part XVII — Official Language
part17.subtitle: Articles 343–351
part17.core: Official-language framework of the Union, States and courts, with protections for linguistic diversity.
points: Hindi in Devanagari script is official language of Union under Art. 343.
English continues for official purposes under parliamentary law.
Eighth Schedule currently contains 22 languages.
part17.upsc: Avoid confusing ‘official language’ with ‘national language’—the Constitution does not declare a national language.

part18.title: Part XVIII — Emergency Provisions
part18.subtitle: Articles 352–360
part18.core: National Emergency, President’s Rule and Financial Emergency.
points: Art. 352: war, external aggression or armed rebellion.
Art. 356: failure of constitutional machinery in a State.
Art. 360: Financial Emergency; never proclaimed so far.
part18.upsc: 44th Amendment safeguards + S.R. Bommai limits on Art. 356 are essential.

part19.title: Part XIX — Miscellaneous
part19.subtitle: Articles 361–367
part19.core: Miscellaneous provisions including protections for President/Governors and interpretation provisions.
points: Art. 361: certain immunities of President and Governors while in office.
Art. 366 contains definitions.
Art. 367 concerns interpretation.
part19.upsc: Often appears as statement-based Prelims material.

part20.title: Part XX — Amendment of Constitution
part20.subtitle: Article 368
part20.core: Procedure and power to amend the Constitution, constrained by the judicially evolved Basic Structure doctrine.
points: Three broad routes: simple majority outside Art. 368; special majority; special majority + ratification by at least half of States for federal provisions.
Kesavananda Bharati (1973): Basic Structure cannot be destroyed.
Judicial review of amendments remains possible.
part20.upsc: One of the highest-yield constitutional topics for both Prelims and Mains.

part21.title: Part XXI — Temporary, Transitional & Special Provisions
part21.subtitle: Articles 369–392
part21.core: Temporary/transitional provisions and special arrangements for various States.
points: Includes Art. 371 series special provisions for several States.
Art. 370 text remains in Constitution but its operative legal position changed following 2019 measures and subsequent Supreme Court adjudication.
Useful for asymmetric federalism.
part21.upsc: Treat special provisions as examples of differentiated/asymmetric federalism.

part22.title: Part XXII — Short Title, Commencement, Hindi Text & Repeals
part22.subtitle: Articles 393–395
points: Art. 393: short title.
Art. 394: commencement.
Art. 394A: authoritative Hindi text; Art. 395: repeals.
part22.upsc: Low frequency, useful for elimination-based MCQs.

sch1.title: First Schedule
sch1.subtitle: States and Union Territories
sch1.core: Names and territorial descriptions of States and Union Territories.
points: Closely linked with Arts. 1–4.
Changes may accompany State reorganisation.

sch5.title: Fifth Schedule
sch5.subtitle: Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes
sch5.core: Administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in specified areas.
points: Governor has special responsibilities.
Tribes Advisory Council is important.
Different from Sixth Schedule autonomous councils.

sch6.title: Sixth Schedule
sch6.subtitle: Tribal Areas in four North-Eastern States
sch6.core: Autonomous District/Regional Councils in tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
points: Legislative/judicial/financial powers in specified fields.
Not applicable to every North-Eastern State.

sch7.title: Seventh Schedule
sch7.subtitle: Union, State and Concurrent Lists
sch7.core: Three legislative lists distribute subjects between Parliament and State legislatures.
points: Union List, State List, Concurrent List.
Residuary legislative power lies with Parliament.
Repugnancy in Concurrent field is governed principally by Art. 254.

sch8.title: Eighth Schedule
sch8.subtitle: 22 languages
sch8.core: Recognised scheduled languages of the Constitution.
points: Currently 22 languages.
English is not in the Eighth Schedule.
Being scheduled does not make a language the ‘national language’.

sch10.title: Tenth Schedule
sch10.subtitle: Anti-defection
sch10.core: Disqualification of legislators on ground of defection.
points: Added by 52nd Amendment (1985).
Decision is made by Speaker/Chairman, subject to judicial review.
91st Amendment removed split exception and strengthened anti-defection framework.
sch10.upsc: Mains debate: stability vs deliberative freedom.

sch11.title: Eleventh Schedule
sch11.subtitle: 29 Panchayat subjects
sch11.core: 29 functional subjects that may be devolved to Panchayats.
points: Added by 73rd Amendment.
Devolution depends substantially on State legislation.

sch12.title: Twelfth Schedule
sch12.subtitle: 18 Municipal functions
sch12.core: 18 functional areas that may be entrusted to Municipalities.
points: Added by 74th Amendment.
Includes urban planning, roads, water supply, sanitation and more.

schedules: Territorial description of States and Union Territories.
Emoluments/allowances and provisions concerning specified constitutional authorities.
Allocation of seats in the Council of States.
Administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes.
Autonomous arrangements in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
Historically used to shield listed laws; subject to Basic Structure review after I.R. Coelho.
amendments: Added, among other changes, Art. 15(4), Arts. 31A–31B and Ninth Schedule; also altered speech-related restrictions.
Major State reorganisation-era constitutional changes; reorganised constitutional classification of States/UTs.
Affirmed Parliament’s constituent power to amend and made presidential assent to an Art. 368 amendment bill mandatory.
Introduced Art. 31C in its original form and altered property-right provisions.
‘Mini-Constitution’: Preamble additions, Fundamental Duties, tribunals and wide institutional changes.
Reversed several Emergency-era changes; replaced ‘internal disturbance’ with ‘armed rebellion’; strengthened liberty safeguards.
Constitutionalised Panchayats; Part IX + Eleventh Schedule.
Constitutionalised Municipalities; Part IXA + Twelfth Schedule.
Inserted Art. 21A (education 6–14), modified Art. 45 and added Art. 51A(k).
Strengthened anti-defection rules and capped size of Councils of Ministers at 15% (subject to minimum for States).
Co-operative societies: Art. 19(1)(c), Art. 43B and Part IXB; Part IXB later partly invalidated for State co-operatives by SC (2021).
Introduced GST constitutional framework, including GST Council.
Constitutional status to NCBC; inserted Art. 338B and 342A framework.
Enabled up to 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections under Arts. 15(6) and 16(6).
Extended SC/ST legislative reservation; ended Anglo-Indian nominated-seat provision at the relevant level.
Restored/clarified States’ power to identify SEBCs for their own purposes.
Provides one-third reservation for women in Lok Sabha, State Assemblies and Delhi Assembly; operation is linked to a future delimitation after the first census taken after commencement.
cases: Kesavananda Bharati v State of Kerala
Basic Structure
Parliament’s amendment power is broad but cannot destroy the Constitution’s Basic Structure.
Maneka Gandhi v Union of India
Article 21
Procedure affecting life/liberty must be fair, just and reasonable; Arts. 14, 19 and 21 became deeply interconnected.
Minerva Mills v Union of India
FR–DPSP Balance
Limited amending power and harmony between Fundamental Rights and DPSPs are constitutionally fundamental.
S.R. Bommai v Union of India
Article 356 / Federalism
President’s Rule is judicially reviewable; floor test and federal/secular principles gained central importance.
I.R. Coelho v State of Tamil Nadu
Ninth Schedule
Post-24 April 1973 Ninth Schedule laws can be tested against Basic Structure through their impact on core rights.
Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Assn. v Union of India
NJAC
99th Amendment/NJAC struck down; judicial independence treated as part of Basic Structure.
K.S. Puttaswamy v Union of India
Privacy
Privacy recognised as a Fundamental Right under the liberty/dignity framework.
Janhit Abhiyan v Union of India
EWS Reservation
Supreme Court upheld the 103rd Amendment enabling EWS reservation.
Government of NCT of Delhi v Union of India
Delhi Governance
Clarified representative government, aid-and-advice and control questions in the NCT’s special constitutional framework.
